title: Root saturation and fractional column replacement strictly lower a determinant
statement:
Let $r\geq1$ and let $S\subseteq\mathbf Z^r$ be an additive submonoid, meaning $0\in S$ and $s+t\in S$ for $s,t\in S$. Assume $S$ is root saturated in $\mathbf Z^r$: for $n\in\mathbf N$, $n>0$, and $t\in\mathbf Z^r$, $nt\in S$ implies $t\in S$. Let $A$ be an integer $r\times r$ matrix whose columns $v_i$ lie in $S$, with $\det A\ne0$ [def-weil-pbc-matrix-determinant]. Let $a\in\mathbf Q^r$ satisfy $0\leq a_i<1$ for every $i$ and suppose $x=\sum_i a_i v_i$ lies in $\mathbf Z^r$. Then $x\in S$. For every index $j$ with $a_j>0$, the integer matrix $A'$ obtained by replacing column $j$ of $A$ by $x$ has all columns in $S$ and satisfies, in $\mathbf Q$,
$$\det A'=a_j\det A,\qquad 0<|\det A'|=a_j|\det A|<|\det A|.$$

source.place: Algebra, Tag 0F0K (algebra-item-cauchy-binet, algebra.tex lines 282--288), square case; the one-column identity follows from the Leibniz formula. Root saturation is the convention of ILO VIII 3.1.17, printed p. 101. The denominator and strict-descent argument is agent-supplied. Extracts old proof step 6 of lem-trf-fs-chart-free-factorization.

proof.text: Set N equal to the finite product of the positive reduced denominators of the coefficients. For each i, its denominator divides N; write N = den(a_i) d_i and put b_i = d_i num(a_i).toNat. Nonnegativity of a_i implies that its numerator is nonnegative, so (N : Q) a_i = b_i. Multiply each coordinate equation by N, distribute the sum, and use injectivity of Z -> Q to obtain N • x = sum_i b_i • column_i(A) in the integer lattice. Additive-submonoid closure puts this sum in S; apply NSMulSaturated and N > 0 to conclude x in S.

source.place: VIII 3.1.17, printed p. 101, saturation convention only; the common-denominator calculation is agent-supplied, as in the original node.

proof.text: For a fixed j with a_j > 0, split on i = j to see that every column of updateCol j x belongs to S. Map A to Q. The given coordinate equations identify the replacement column with the rational linear combination of the original columns. Apply Mathlib Matrix.det_updateCol_sum, which already proves the multilinearity and repeated-column calculation. Int.cast_det identifies the mapped determinants with the casts of the integer determinants, yielding det(A.updateCol j x) = a_j det A.

source.place: Tag 0F0K, algebra-item-cauchy-binet, lines 282–288, determinant context only; the calculation uses Matrix.det_updateCol_sum in Mathlib/LinearAlgebra/Matrix/Determinant/Basic.lean:435–439, and the strict inequalities are elementary.

proof.text: Injectivity of the integer cast makes det A nonzero in Q, hence D = |det A| > 0. The identity and abs_mul give |det(A.updateCol j x)| = a_j D since a_j > 0. Positivity of both factors gives a positive replacement determinant in absolute value, and multiplying a_j < 1 by D gives strict descent.
